 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1988, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of the (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 deceased Sri.Pradeep.N S/o Nagaraju, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 29.04.2022 at about 07.50 to 07.52 p.m, deceased Pradeep.N was riding his Motor Bike bearing No.KA-42-EC-4779 along with his friend Kiran as a pillion rider on Sathanoor - Doddahalahalli Road, near Yedamaranahalli Lake, Uyyamballi Hobli,
at the time one Tractor bearing No.KA-09-T-4898 driven by its driver, at very high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and took extreme of the road and dashed against the deceased Motor Bike.
Due to this he fell down along with his vehicle and sustained grievous injuries on his head, hands, legs and other injuries all over the body and died on the spot itself.
The petitioners have spent Rs.1,25,000/- towards transportation of deadbody, funeral and last rites.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the parents and petitioner No.4 is the minor daughter of the deceased.
Prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 27 years and was doing agriculture work and also doing milk vending business and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to accidental death (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 of the deceased, the petitioners put to great hardship, mental agony and they lost sole earning member of the family have also loss of love and affection towards deceased.
The accident is occurred due to the rash and negligent act of driver of offending Tractor and in this regard the Sathanoor Police have filed a case against driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the RC Owner of offending vehicle

,
are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- along with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and with costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.2 did not appeared and hence, he was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denies the existence of insurance policy in respect of the vehicle bearing No.KA-09-T-4898 of the respondent No.2 and the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending Tractor, age,
income, occupation of the deceased and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and Ranjitha.

Act.

The compensation claimed is exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues are framed by my learned predecessor:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners proves that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Pradeep.N S/o Nagaraju?

Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Pradeep.N S/o Nagaraju was died out of RTA alleged to have been taken place on 29.04.2022 at about 7.50 to 7.52 p.m,
on Sathnur - Doddalahalli Road, near Yadamaranahalli Lake, Uyyamballi Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Tractor bearing registration No.KA-09-T-4898 by its driver as alleged in the petition ?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got examined one eye-witness as PW.2 and through them got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 and closed their side evidence.
On the otherhand, Manager Legal of the respondent No.1 Insurance Company got examined as RW.1 and no documents have been marked and closed its side evidence.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsels for the petitioners.
Despite sufficient opportunity, the respondent No.1 has not advanced its arguments, hence respondent No.1 arguments is taken as heard and perused the records.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS 09. Issue No.1 & 2:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
10. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 is examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments therein.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.1 counsel she clearly stated that petitioner No.4 is her daughter and petitioners No.2 and 3 are her in-laws and denied to the suggestion that her husband was not having Driving licence and he do not know how to ride the Motor Cycle and this accident occurred due to negligence of her husband and also denied to the (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 suggestion that in order to get compensation eventhough accident occurred due to negligence of her husband, false case is registered against the tractor driver.
11.

Further, PW.2 is said to be eye-witness to the accident, he also deposed about rash and negligent driving of offending Tractor by its driver, causing accident and death of deceased in the road traffic accident.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.1 counsel he denied to the suggestion that the tractor was going very slowly and admits that after accident the tractor was standing there and denied to the suggestion that the deceased who had no driving licence has riding his Motor Cycle in the middle of the road in a zig-zag manner and caused accident and also denied to the suggestion that he is not witnessed the accident.
12.
Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 on their behalf.

Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Sathanoor Police, against driver of Tractor bearing No.KA-09-T-4898 for his rash and negligent driving and causing accident, causing grievous injuries and death of deceased.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint lodged against driver of offending Tractor.
Ex.P.3 is copy of (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Notice U/Sec 133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending vehicle.
Ex.P.5 is copy of IMV report which shows involvement of both vehicles in the road traffic accident and both vehicles are damaged.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Inquest Mahazar of deceased Pradeep.N.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Post mortem report of deceased Pradeep.N, wherein it is stated caused of death is due to shock and haemorrhage as a result of head injury sustained.

Ex.P.8 is copy of Charge sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending Tractor for his rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and causing accident, causing grievous injuries and causing death of deceased.
Ex.P.9 is copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner No.1.

On going through the above oral and documentary evidence, the petitioners have proved and established that the deceased Pradeep.N was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 29.04.2022 at about 07.50 to 07.52 p.m, on Sathanoor - Doddahalahalli Road, near Yedamaranahalli Lake, Uyyamballi Hobli, due to rash and negligent driving of Tractor bearing No.KA-09-T-4898, by its driver, as alleged in the petition.

It is also further proved that petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are parents and petitioner No.4 is the minor daughter of deceased and they are legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased.
Accordingly, these Issues No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Pradeep.N, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

PW.1/petitioner No.1 who is the wife of the deceased has stated that as on the date of alleged accident the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 27 years and was doing agriculture work and also doing milk vending business and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.

Due to accidental death of the (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 deceased, the petitioners put to great hardship, mental agony,
loss of love and affection and they lost sole earning member of the family and they have spent Rs.1,25,000/- towards transportation of deadbody, funeral and last rites.
15. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any Birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.

However, they have produced Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card of deceased, but said document is not authenticated document to proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence regarding his date of birth, said document can be taken into consideration, according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 30.05.1995 and alleged accident was occurred on 29.04.2022
, it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is 27 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 27 years.
As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors.

(SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 26 to 30 years is 17.
16.
So far as avocation and income of deceased is concerned, petitioners have not produced any documents or evidence.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding avocation and income of deceased, this tribunal has placed reliance upon notional income as per the chart issued by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru, the notional income as per the year 2022 is Ranjitha.

Therefore, this Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
17.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In otherwords, there are 4 dependents and as per law, 1/4th of the income should be deduct towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.

Since deceased was aged about 27 years at the time of accident, 40%
income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (15,500 + 6,200) = (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 Rs.21,700/-.

Since there are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (21,700 - 5,425) =
Rs.16,275/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.16,275/-.
As the deceased was aged about 27 years, the multiplier of 17 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.33,20,100/- (Rs.16,275 x 12 x 17) towards loss of dependency.

18. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses,
10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
19. The claimant No.1 is the wife, claimants No.2 and 3 are the parents and claimant No.4 is the daughter of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.48,000/- towards loss of spousal consortium.

The claimants No.2 and 3 are entitled for (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 Rs.48,000/- each towards loss of filial consortium and claimants No.4 is entitled for Rs.48,000/-
towards loss of parental consortium.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/4th of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;

. Accordingly, I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.35,48,100/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Regarding liability:-
In this case, the respondent No.2 is placed exparte.
On behalf of the respondent No.1, its Manager Legal is examined as RW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the written statement averments therein.

During the course of cross-examination by the petitioners counsel, she admits that as on the date of accident the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid and in in force and she has not seen the accident and also admits that the Police have filed Charge sheet against their insured vehicle and respondent No.1 in its written statement has not specifically denied the issuance of policy in favour of offending Tractor and there is no evidence on record to show that the owner or driver have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

Hence, as per the averments made in the (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 petition and as admitted by the RW.1 in her cross-examination, the insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force and further, as per Charge sheet there is no whisper regarding driving of the offending Tractor by its driver without insurance policy or driving licence.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the R.C. Owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.35,48,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.4

: In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.35,48,100/- (Rupees Thirty five lakhs forty eight thousand and one hundred only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since the petitioner No.4 is minor, on deposit of the award amount with interest, the entire share amount of the petitioner No.4 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till she attain age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 name of minor petitioner No.4 by her guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner No.4.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

However, they have produced Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card of deceased, but said document is not authenticated document to proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence regarding his date of birth, said document can be taken into consideration, according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 30.05.1995 and alleged accident was occurred on 29.04.2022
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 27 years.
Since there are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (21,700 - 5,425) =
Rs.16,275/-.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/4th of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
 Sl. Head of Amount in  No. Compensation Rs.
 1. Loss of Dependency 33,20,100-00  (After deducting 1/4th of  the income towards  personal and living  expenses)
 2. Loss of spousal 48,000-00  consortium (petitioner  No.1)
 3. Loss of filial consortium 96,000-00  (petitioners No.2 and 3)
 4. Loss of parental 48,000-00  consortium (petitioners Ranjitha.N.S vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51088569/
6  No.4)
 5. Loss of estate 18,000-00  (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.2759/2022  6. Funeral expenses and 18,000-00  transportation of dead  body
Hence, as per the averments made in the (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 petition and as admitted by the RW.1 in her cross-examination, the insurance policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force and further, as per Charge sheet there is no whisper regarding driving of the offending Tractor by its driver without insurance policy or driving licence.
Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the R.C. Owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.35,48,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.35,48,100/- (Rupees Thirty five lakhs forty eight thousand and one hundred only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioners No.1 to 3 are entitled to get release 70% each of the award through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% each shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
Since the petitioner No.4 is minor, on deposit of the award amount with interest, the entire share amount of the petitioner No.4 shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Schedule Bank till she attain age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.2759/2022 name of minor petitioner No.4 by her guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor petitioner No.4.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
